title: Jackson Ward through time
about: Jackson Ward before and after the Richmond-Petersburg Turnpike (cleared 1955-58, opened 1958). Each scene draws the buildings standing today that had been built by its year (OSM start_date, else the City of Richmond assessor's year built), plus buildings traced from the Sanborn map of 1952, volume 3 (Leigh Street north to the railroad), and from the earlier downtown tracings south of Leigh. Before 1955 the ground inside the highway's trench is an estimate rebuilt from its edges (see the ground note). Rough draft: not for publication.

epochs.title: Before the Turnpike
epochs.note: The last Sanborn survey before the Richmond-Petersburg Turnpike was cut through the ward in 1955-58. Buildings north of Leigh Street are traced from the 1952 volume 3 sheets; south of Leigh from the 1924-25 and 1950-52 volume 1 tracings. Rough draft.

epochs.title: After the road (about 1960)
epochs.note: A year after the Turnpike opened (July 1, 1958). Traced 1952 buildings whose center falls in the highway's corridor polygon (today's paved roadway and ramps plus 15 m each side, a stand-in for the 1958 right-of-way) are gone from 1956 (tools/sanborn/jw/corridor_ends.py); those outside it are drawn standing, because when each was lost is not yet dated. Beyond the corridor this is an approximation: later clearances (the Coliseum, the 1970s renewal, Gilpin Court's additions of 1957 and 1970) are not yet dated building by building. Drawn as 1959 so that buildings whose end is assumed (1960, the downtown series' rule) still stand.

ground.name: Ramp banks at the I-64 junction, before 1955
ground.note: Estimate. East of 1st Street the interchange ramps stand on the old plateau rim above Shockoe Valley. The USGS Richmond sheet surveyed 1933-34 shows ground there at about the height the lidar measures today (its 150-foot contour, labeled near the valley rim, falls where today's does), so the ground is kept as measured, except that banks narrower than 50 m (the ramps' embankments, up to 9 m high) are taken down to the ground beside them. The ravine the sheet shows heading into the plateau north of the junction, and the valley side under I-95 south of it, are not rebuilt: the lidar is kept there.

ground.note: Estimate, not a survey. The Richmond-Petersburg Turnpike (1955-58) runs through the ward in a trench up to about 8 m deep (3 to 6.5 m where the old cross streets ran). Inside this outline the lidar is set aside and the ground rebuilt as the smoothest surface (a membrane) that meets the measured ground at the outline and carries each street listed here through at grade, straight between its surviving ends. The outline is today's motorway and ramp ways (OpenStreetMap) buffered 22 m (10 m for ramps), widened over the cut slopes the lidar shows (slopes over 12% within 60 m of a motorway), and simplified; east of 1st and Duval streets it keeps only the main line (30 m either side). Checked by moving the outline onto undisturbed plateau nearby (0.3-1.1 m RMS) and against the USGS Richmond sheet surveyed 1933-34 (10-foot contours: no contour can be read near seven points along the trench, and the rebuilt ground would move at most 0.8 m to agree). Error about 1.5 m (95%) mid-trench, 3 m at its ends; a small ravine the sheet shows near 7th Street is not rebuilt (ground.md in the story folder).

atGrade.note: Streets and walks that cross the Turnpike on bridges today crossed level ground before it was cut (the USGS Richmond sheet of 1934 shows them as ordinary streets); before 1958 they are drawn at grade.
Fifth and Seventh streets cross East Leigh Street on bridges built in 1971; before them the streets are drawn meeting at grade (approximate).

leaveOut.why: 28 of its 57 traced buildings fall on the Capitol Square lawn, a public square since the Capitol was built (https://vga.virginia.gov/?p=73), so the sheet's fit (read by eye) is wrong; its other buildings are taken to be out of place too. Left out until the sheet is placed again.
3 of its 5 traced buildings fall on the Capitol Square lawn: the same misfit as sheet 5.

rules.note: I-64 east of its junction with the Turnpike, and its ramps, carry start_date 1968 in OpenStreetMap; Roads to the Future gives 1968 for I-64's completion through Richmond. Before then not drawn (the 1959 scene shows the Turnpike alone).

The Fifth Street Viaduct over Bacon's Quarter Branch and the railroad: the first opened in 1891, a reinforced-concrete one in 1933, and today's in 1997 (the National Bridge Inventory gives 1996). A viaduct stood here in 1952; it is drawn in today's form.

Today's North 1st Street bridge over the CSX railroad and Bacon Street was built in 2000 (National Bridge Inventory). The USGS Richmond sheets surveyed 1933-34 and revised 1956 show 1st Street running straight across the railroad and the valley here; the earlier crossing's form was not found. Drawn in today's form (approximate).

Today's Chamberlayne bridge over the CSX railroad was built in 1992 (National Bridge Inventory). The USGS sheets of 1933-34 and 1956 show Chamberlayne Parkway crossing the railroad here; the earlier crossing's form was not found. Drawn in today's form (approximate).

count.note: The count picture: buildings traced from the 1952 Sanborn sheets whose center falls in the highway's paved footprint (today's roadway and ramps) in the darker tone, in the corridor (paved plus 15 m each side) in the lighter, every other building quiet, and both outlines. Polygons from tools/sanborn/jw/footprint.py; counts in tools/sanborn/jw/counts.json.

streets.note: The lost streets picture: the curated stretches of street the Turnpike took drawn in the mark's tone, the corridor outlined, buildings quiet; in today's scene the decks of the bridges that carry the surviving streets over the trench in the same tone.
